title: Context-pack freshness stamp on handoff bundles and prime
description: Context: a 2h47m dabble-employee-app agent session made 300 CLI calls with 24 failures. Failure clusters: 117 read-only work show polls (~40% of all calls), 14 identical failed sync refresh retries, 6 vault init retries, 66 agent finish calls with only 2 standalone evidence records, 6 NOT_FOUND finish/release (ownership confusion), 1 CONFLICT claim, 2 POLICY_VIOLATION sprint closes. Design principle for this mission: every response (success or error) must carry enough state that the correct next action is derivable without another read, and the honest path (evidence, ownership, health) must be the path of least resistance. Problem: agents were told to trust their handoff bundle and stop polling, but had no verifiable reason to — nothing said whether the bundle was still current. Change: stamp context packs / handoff bundles (returned by work claim and agent start) with the ledger sequence at composition time (depends on the H1 ledger-seq task), and make bwrk prime --json report pack-seq vs current ledger seq so an agent can see pack current as of seq N, ledger at seq N and skip re-reads, or see the delta and refresh once. Where: context-pack composition in packages/engine/src/runtime.ts, prime output, docs. Constraint: additive fields only; the stamp must use the same ledger-derived seq as the response envelopes so comparisons are meaningful.
acceptanceCriteria: Handoff bundles carry the ledger seq at composition time
prime --json reports bundle seq versus current ledger seq
Seq semantics are identical to the response-envelope seq (shared implementation, test proves equality)
